subject.title: Slack DM threads still serialize in 2026.7.1; add configurable per-thread session scope

question: Should Slack support an opt-in per-thread DM session contract despite the shipped stable shared-DM session behavior?
rationale: The request adds a new configuration surface and changes session continuity, transcript ownership, concurrency, and command semantics; source inspection cannot choose which Slack DM mental model the product should support.

options.title: Add Opt-In Thread Scope
options.body: Keep `shared` as the default and add a Slack-owned `thread` mode with explicit compatibility and end-to-end session-routing coverage.

options.title: Keep Shared Sessions
options.body: Retain the existing stable DM session contract and document that independent parallel tasks require separate channels, agents, or explicit runtime bindings.

options.title: Design Generic Execution Lanes
options.body: Pause Slack-specific configuration and first design a channel-neutral way to run parallel execution lanes without splitting conversation sessions.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Thread Scope
recommendation.body: Keep `shared` as the default and add a Slack-owned `thread` mode with explicit compatibility and end-to-end session-routing coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows direct involvement in establishing, fixing, documenting, and merging the current Slack DM session contract.
